correctness.rationale: For the frozen Erlang reversal model, the two-run affine map preserves [0,2], maps it into (0,2), and couples starts by a product of independent factors BC with negative mean logarithm. Equilibrium sampling of either sign has probability 1/2 and biases the current duration only, not the entrance deficit. Checked the critical moment: the bound (U+V)^(-p) ≤ U^(-(p−q))V^(-q), with U=2(1−B) and V=BCZ′, has finite B factor at small durations if p−q<m, and finite B and C factors at large durations if q<β. Starting with any p<m and taking steps of size at most min(m/2,β/2) reaches β with only strictly subcritical intermediate q. Integrating the ordinary Erlang survivor and dividing by m/λ gives the leading equilibrium-age term e^(−λt)(λt)^(m−1)/(m(m−1)!), hence the stated factor β^(m−1)/(2m(m−1)!). The normalized positive-age integral is dominated by a constant times Z^(−β) since Z≤2, and Pr(Z≤ε)=o(ε^β). The ordinary-run survivor gives the analogous end-of-positive-run small-ball asymptotic; negative runs contribute only when their independent equilibrium age is O(ε) and their starting deficit is at most 2ε. Symmetry and the distinct powers m/(κτ) give the left edge and fixed-mean ordering. Audited frozen RESULT.md, metadata, audit/review, verification and checker source; the reported finite checks were not rerun and are not a limit certificate.

value.rationale: Rare occupancy of the propulsion-supported edge is a natural stationary observable. The exact leading coefficient and logarithmic multiplicity distinguish Erlang phase counts at identical mean times, where a mean-based approximation loses the ordering. Proving critical entrance-gap integrability is substantive, not a substitution of an exponential rate into the known beta distribution. The theorem does not claim uniformity over shapes or thermal robustness.
